advances: The fixed calibration is impossible before the middle-slice midpoint stage: no two-dimensional convex \(A_0\) can realize the prescribed positive lower cells \(P_{\{1\}},P_{\{2\}},P_{\{1,3\}},P_{\{2,3\}}\), with every other lower cell null, for one affine triple whose sum is constant and whose shifted sum is positive. Hence there is no full realization satisfying the registered hypotheses, and the requested middle-multiplicity inequality holds vacuously. This closes only this fixed calibration; it does not supply the proposed quantitative midpoint bound for a realizable lower-cell table.
author: r105_five_cap_fixed_chain
proof:
Set
\[
h_j=\lambda_j+s_j
\qquad(j=1,2,3)
\]
and
\[
c=h_1+h_2+h_3
=1+s_1+s_2+s_3>2.
\tag{1}
\]
Membership in \(C_{0j}\) is exactly the weak inequality \(h_j\ge0\).
Let \(U=\operatorname{int}A_0\). Since \(A_0\) is two-dimensional and
convex, \(U\) is a nonempty open convex set, and the polygonal boundary
\(\partial A_0\) has planar area zero. Each zero set
\[
L_j=\{h_j=0\}
\]
is a line and therefore has planar area zero.

First we extract the qualitative chamber obstruction, including the
possibility of crossing two cutting lines simultaneously. The prescribed
support contains no label having both \(1\) and \(2\), and no label having
neither \(1\) nor \(2\). Hence
\[
U\cap\{h_1>0,\ h_2>0\}=\varnothing,
\qquad
U\cap\{h_1<0,\ h_2<0\}=\varnothing.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, either displayed set, if nonempty, is open. After removing the
null line \(L_3\), it is a union of exact cells whose labels are absent
from the prescribed support. It would therefore be a nonempty open set
of area zero, which is impossible. Thus
\[
h_1(z)h_2(z)\le0\qquad(z\in U).
\tag{3}
\]

The positive areas of \(P_{\{1\}}\) and \(P_{\{2\}}\), together with the
nullity of the three cutting lines, give points \(p,q\in U\) outside all
three lines such that
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
 &h_1&h_2&h_3\\ \hline
p&>0&<0&<0\\
q&<0&>0&<0.
\end{array}
\tag{4}
\]
In particular, \(h_1\) takes both signs on \(U\), so \(L_1\cap U\)
contains a nondegenerate line segment. For every \(z\in L_1\cap U\),
one must have \(h_2(z)=0\). If \(h_2(z)>0\), continuity and the fact that
the nonconstant affine function \(h_1\) takes both signs in every
neighborhood of a point of \(L_1\) would produce a nearby point with
\(h_1>0,h_2>0\), contrary to (2). If \(h_2(z)<0\), the same argument on
the other side of \(L_1\) would produce \(h_1<0,h_2<0\), again contrary
to (2).

Thus \(h_2\) vanishes on a nondegenerate segment of \(L_1\). Since
\(h_2\) is a nonconstant affine function, its zero line equals \(L_1\).
Two nonconstant affine functions with the same zero line are nonzero
scalar multiples. Their opposite signs at \(p\) show that the scalar is
negative, so for some \(\alpha>0\),
\[
h_2=-\alpha h_1.
\tag{5}
\]
This proves that a simultaneous two-line crossing cannot bypass a
missing positive-area chamber: the null chambers force the two lines to
coincide, not merely to meet at one point.

Combining (1) and (5) now gives the exact one-dimensional form
\[
h_3=c-h_1-h_2
=c+(\alpha-1)h_1.
\tag{6}
\]
At the point \(p\) from (4), one has \(h_1(p)>0\) and \(h_3(p)<0\).
Because \(c>0\), (6) forces
\[
\alpha-1<0.
\tag{7}
\]
At the point \(q\), one has \(h_1(q)<0\) and \(h_3(q)<0\). Equation
(6), again using \(c>0\), instead forces
\[
\alpha-1>0.
\tag{8}
\]
Equations (7) and (8) contradict each other.

Therefore the prescribed lower-cell table cannot occur in one common
affine arrangement on a two-dimensional convex \(A_0\). Adding
\(A_1,A_2\), midpoint compatibility, upper emptiness, or row capacities
cannot restore a nonexistent lower arrangement. Hence no full
realization of the registered calibration exists, which proves the
stated consequence.
statement:
Let \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\) be nonconstant affine functions on an affine plane such that
\[
\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=1,
\]
and let \(s_1,s_2,s_3\in\mathbb R\) satisfy
\[
s_1+s_2+s_3>1.
\]
Let \(A_0\) be a compact two-dimensional convex polygon, put
\[
C_{0j}=A_0\cap\{\lambda_j\ge -s_j\},
\]
and, for \(I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}\), let
\[
P_I=\left\{z\in A_0:
\{j:z\in C_{0j}\}=I\right\}.
\]
There is no such data satisfying
\[
|P_{\{1\}}|=\frac9{100},\qquad
|P_{\{2\}}|=\frac1{25},\qquad
|P_{\{1,3\}}|=\frac3{500},\qquad
|P_{\{2,3\}}|=\frac{57}{500},
\]
and \(|P_I|=0\) for every other \(I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}\).

Consequently, there are no compact two-dimensional convex polygons
\(A_0,A_1,A_2\), affine functions, and slopes satisfying all the
hypotheses of the registered fixed-chain calibration. In particular,
every such full realization satisfies
\[
\sum_{j=1}^3
\left|A_1\cap\{\lambda_j\ge0\}\right|-1
\ge\frac1{300}.
\]
